.engramdb/memories/staging-export-bucket-points-at-the-prod-bucket_01a0f6dc-beec-7eb2-ae37-74a6815fc1b7.md:15:In staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the production bucket. Never run scripts/export.py against staging without `--dry-run`.

Yes, but only with `--dry-run`.

A project memory says that in staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the production bucket. It also says never to run `scripts/export.py` against staging without `--dry-run`. A real staging run could write to prod.

```
python scripts/export.py --env staging --dry-run
```

The script currently only reads `EXPORT_BUCKET` and prints a line. It doesn't branch on `--dry-run`, and it doesn't write anything yet. The flag is a safeguard for when the export logic is added, not something that protects you today.

I haven't run it. I also haven't checked what `EXPORT_BUCKET` is set to in your staging shell, since the repo doesn't define it. Before any non-dry run, run `echo $EXPORT_BUCKET` and confirm it isn't the prod bucket. Alternatively, override it with a dedicated staging bucket.

I can run the dry run for you if you'd like.
